response.why: Kaito's 0 ability (surveil 2 + draw a card since the opponent lost life this turn) is pure value with no downside right now - card selection plus a guaranteed card draw. The +1 emblem only buffs Kaito himself (my one Ninja) marginally, and -2 stunning a blocker has no immediate payoff since combat is already over this turn. Passing wastes the once-per-turn loyalty activation entirely.
response.plan: Activate Kaito's 0 ability for surveil 2 and a card draw. Hold Faerie Mastermind, Floodpits Drowner, Preacher, and Bat in hand for future turns; Kaito is hexproof on my turns so I don't need to protect him further right now.

response.why: Floodpits Drowner (2/1, no deathtouch) and Preacher of the Schism (2/4 deathtouch) are both attacking; Floodpits Drowner has vigilance so it stayed untapped. Blocking Drowner with the Vampire Token trades my expendable 1/1 for their real 2/1 creature (mutual kill) while eating only the unblocked Preacher's 2 damage - a clean value trade. Blocking the deathtouch Preacher instead just loses my token for nothing since Preacher survives at 4 toughness; taking no blocks eats 4 total damage for no gain.
response.plan: Block Floodpits Drowner with the Vampire Token to trade for it; take 2 unblocked from Preacher of the Schism (fine at 19 life vs their 15). Continue developing next turn with Preacher, Faerie Mastermind, or Enduring Curiosity.

response.why: Kaito's -2 (tap + double stun counter on target creature) can lock down their only real blocker, Preacher of the Schism, for free - opening a fully unblocked attack this turn with my Preacher (2/4) and Kaito (3/4) for 5 damage plus Preacher's vampire-token and card-draw triggers, with zero mana cost. That's a bigger swing than any spell I could cast right now. Playing the tapped Undercity Sewers is free value for the land drop, and Enduring Curiosity is the best spell to follow up with using my 4 mana (draws a card off every combat hit from Preacher/Kaito). Casting Faerie Mastermind/Floodpits Drowner now wastes their flash value, and activating Kaito's 0 ability precombat draws nothing since no one has lost life yet this turn.
response.plan: Activate Kaito's -2 to tap and stun their Preacher of the Schism, removing their only blocker. Play the tapped Undercity Sewers for the free land drop. Attack with Preacher and Kaito unblocked for a big hit plus Preacher's triggers. Postcombat, cast Enduring Curiosity with the 4 mana, and activate Kaito's 0 ability for surveil 2 + a card draw since the opponent will have lost life this turn.

response.why: Opponent is fully tapped out right now and their only creature (Preacher) is already tapped while their Kaito isn't a creature on my turn - so I have zero risk of a countered spell or a blocked attacker this combat regardless of what I do. Casting Enduring Curiosity precombat is clearly best: it doesn't need to attack to trigger, so putting it into play now means its 'draw a card when a creature you control deals combat damage' fires off BOTH Preacher and Kaito connecting unblocked this turn, on top of Preacher's own draw-while-ahead-on-life trigger - a big card-advantage swing, and even if they later Go for the Throat it, it recurs as an enchantment and keeps the draw engine. Floodpits Drowner has no good target right now (their only creature is already tapped) so it's better saved to stun their Kaito before it attacks next turn, and Faerie Mastermind is a low-impact 2/1 that doesn't help this turn's attack.
response.plan: Cast Enduring Curiosity precombat to get its combat-damage draw trigger on this turn's Preacher+Kaito attack (opponent has no legal blockers), then attack with both unblocked. Hold Floodpits Drowner and Faerie Mastermind in hand with flash to ambush-block or stun their Kaito on their turn.

leaves.opp_board: Preacher of the Schism 2/4 T | 4 lands (0 untapped)

response.why: Opponent has zero blockers available right now — their Preacher is tapped and their Kaito isn't a creature on my turn — so attacking with everything is completely free of risk. Attacking all maximizes damage (15->10) and triggers both Preacher's draw and Enduring Curiosity's draw off each attacker's combat damage, growing my hand to 7. Holding back either attacker only loses value with no compensating safety since nothing can block or punish me next turn from an empty board.
response.plan: Attack with both Preacher and Kaito since opponent has no legal blockers this turn; bank the card draws and hold Floodpits Drowner/Faerie Mastermind with flash for their turn to ambush or stun their Kaito.

response.why: I already have a Kaito on the battlefield, so the second Kaito in hand is legend-rule dead unless my first one dies - it's the least useful card to keep versus removal (Go for the Throat), lands, and cheap flash creatures that all still do something.
response.plan: Keep Go for the Throat and the flash creatures (Floodpits Drowner, Faerie Mastermind) up for opponent's turn to answer their Kaito or ambush block; discard the redundant second legendary Kaito.

response.why: It's my upkeep with an empty stack - no reason to commit mana or cards before I even draw for the turn. Opponent is fully tapped out (all 5 lands used on their Preacher + Floodpits Drowner last turn) and stays tapped out through my entire turn regardless of when I act, so there's no safety advantage to acting now versus waiting for precombat main with full information (my draw, and the option to develop mana efficiently). Passing preserves maximum flexibility for no cost.
response.plan: Pass through upkeep/draw and decide what to deploy at precombat main once I've seen my draw - opponent is tapped out for my whole turn so there's no rush. Still holding Go for the Throat and flash creatures to answer their board or ambush block on their turn.

response.why: Opponent is fully tapped out (all 5 lands tapped) so anything I do now is safe from response. Playing a land (Swamp or Island) is free value with no opportunity cost. Casting a second deathtouch Preacher is the strongest spell play - it stacks another deathtouch attacker that trades up against any blocker, and Go for the Throat preemptively removing a blocker also sets up a clean unblocked hit. Faerie Mastermind/Floodpits Drowner/Spyglass Siren are lower-impact right now since there's nothing urgent to answer this turn.
response.plan: Play a land first for the free ramp, then deploy Preacher of the Schism (second deathtouch attacker) or use Go for the Throat to clear a blocker while opponent can't respond, then attack with my deathtouch Preacher - any block trades favorably for me. Keep some instant-speed answers in mind for their turn 12 when they untap with mana.

response.why: Opponent is fully tapped out (0 mana), so this is a free window to develop safely. Playing the land is pure upside. Casting Floodpits Drowner is the standout play: its ETB can tap down their untapped Enduring Curiosity (their best blocker), clearing the way for my Preacher+Enduring Curiosity attack to connect for damage and card draws. Go for the Throat and the small flash creatures are fine but lower-impact than the tempo play of tapping their blocker before combat.
response.plan: Play a land, then flash in Floodpits Drowner targeting their untapped Enduring Curiosity to remove it as a blocker, then attack with Preacher and my Enduring Curiosity. Hold Go for the Throat for a bigger threat later.

response.plan: Hold up Go for the Throat and pass rather than spend it now — their current threats (tapped Preachers, small Drowner/token, recurring Curiosity) aren't worth premium removal. If they cast Sheoldred, the Apocalypse, let it resolve then kill it immediately with Go for the Throat before it drains value. response.why: Kaito, Bane of Nightmares only becomes a creature (and gains hexproof) on its controller's turn — so Go for the Throat is an illegal/wasted target against it whenever it shows up as a 5/6 in these samples; those leaves score low-to-mid since my removal just gets spent on a lesser target instead of doing real work, and 'do nothing' (holding GFT) is better there. Restless Reef's animate ability is the one real danger this turn: it can become a 4/4 deathtouch creature at instant speed (even on my turn) to ambush-block my attackers, and unlike Kaito it's a legal, non-hexproof target once it's actually a creature — so killing it right after the ability resolves (leaf 7) is clearly the best line, clearing a scary deathtouch blocker before I commit to combat. Leaving it up (leaf 8) risks a bad trade against my attackers. Proactively casting Go for the Throat now into their current weak board is mediocre value and burns removal I'd rather keep for Sheoldred or a real Restless Reef activation.
response.plan: Hold Go for the Throat and pass into combat. Kaito can't legally be targeted by removal (hexproof on their turn, noncreature on mine) — that threat has to be handled by blocking with deathtouch Preacher like before, not spent removal. Watch for Restless Reef animating into a 4/4 deathtouch blocker during my attack; if it does, kill it with Go for the Throat right after it resolves as a creature. Otherwise keep attacking with Preacher (deathtouch) + Enduring Curiosity toward their 8 life and save GFT for Sheoldred or another real threat.

response.why: Opponent has only 1 card in hand right now, so Deep-Cavern Bat's ETB (look at their hand, exile a nonland card) is unusually strong this turn — it can strip their entire remaining resource (removal, counterspell, or a bomb) before it ever matters, on top of adding a lifelink flier. That makes the Deep-Cavern Bat leaves score best. Passing/holding mana is fine but doesn't capture that disruption upside; it's still solid since it preserves Go for the Throat for Restless Reef animating into a 4/4 deathtouch blocker (killing it post-resolve, leaf 5, is a clear high-value line) or a real bomb later. Spyglass Siren and proactively casting Go for the Throat now are mediocre — Siren is a small body with minor upside, and none of their current blockers (Floodpits Drowner 2/1, Vampire token, or a hypothetical animated land) justify spending premium removal proactively when Kaito/Sheoldred remain the real long-term problems GFT should answer. Playing an Island is low-impact but not harmful, roughly on par with passing.
response.plan: Cast Deep-Cavern Bat this main phase to strip their last card and add a lifelink flier, since it's a safe window (they're mostly tapped out) and their hand is down to one card. Keep Go for the Throat available for a real threat (Sheoldred, an animated Restless Reef, or whatever they draw) rather than spending it on their current weak blockers. Then move to combat and attack with Preacher (deathtouch) and Enduring Curiosity into their thin blocker set.

response.why: Their hand is empty after I exiled their Preacher of the Schism, so I'm in a dominant, low-risk spot regardless of line: 12 vs 8 life, a much wider board, and they can't do anything until they draw. Playing the Island is strictly better than passing since it's a free land drop with no downside, setting up more mana for future turns (more Deep-Cavern Bats, Go for the Throat, etc.) without giving anything up now. The couple of leaves where they draw into and cast Go for the Throat on my Enduring Curiosity are only mildly worse since it just recurs as an enchantment anyway.
response.plan: Play a land (Island) since it's free value, then move to combat and attack with Preacher of the Schism (deathtouch) and Enduring Curiosity into their thin blocker set (Floodpits Drowner 2/1 and a summoning-sick Vampire token) while they're empty-handed. Keep Go for the Throat for their next real threat (Sheoldred, Kaito, or an animated Restless Reef).

response.why: I'm way ahead (12 vs 8 life, wider board, opponent empty-handed with only two weak blockers left: Floodpits Drowner 2/1 and a summoning-sick Vampire token) and my Preacher has deathtouch, so any block trades favorably for me. Attacking with both creatures has the best floor: even in the worst case (both blockers die trading into my attackers, leaf 2) I lose nothing and strip their remaining blockers for future turns, while other block patterns net real damage and a card draw off Preacher's attack trigger. Holding one attacker back as a blocker (leaves 4/5/7/9) is unnecessarily cautious given my life lead and their empty hand/tapped board — there's no real threat to block against this turn. Not attacking at all wastes the clock against an opponent who can't punish me for over-extending.
response.plan: Attack with both Preacher of the Schism (deathtouch) and Enduring Curiosity. Any block trades in my favor (deathtouch kills anything), and unblocked damage plus Preacher's draw trigger keeps pressuring their 8 life. Keep Go for the Throat in hand for their next real threat since they're currently empty-handed.

response.why: Taking no blocks drops me to 5 life, which is too risky against a deck that still has Sheoldred/Kaito/removal in the deck, even though I keep my whole board — that's the weakest line. Simple chump blocks with a single small creature against a Preacher (Faerie/Floodpits/Siren/Bat each solo-blocking a Preacher) just trade a useful card for minor damage prevention without killing anything, so they're mediocre. Trading a small creature evenly into their Floodpits Drowner (mutual kill) is a better rate since it removes a real utility creature of theirs. The standout is the combined block (leaf 13): double-blocking one Preacher with two small creatures kills it outright (their deathtouch only needs to assign 1 each, but my combined 4 power is exactly lethal to their 4-toughness Preacher), while Deep-Cavern Bat's lifelink trades into and kills their Floodpits Drowner and actually gains me a life — net result: I go UP to 12 life, kill a full Preacher and their Floodpits Drowner, at the cost of three replaceable small bodies while keeping Preacher, Enduring Curiosity, and Spyglass Siren. That's clearly the best outcome available.
response.plan: Block to maximize value: double-block one of their Preachers with two small creatures to kill it, and use Deep-Cavern Bat's lifelink to trade into and kill their Floodpits Drowner, gaining a life in the process. Keep Preacher of the Schism and Enduring Curiosity out of combat as blockers/future attackers. Hold Go for the Throat and Cut Down for their next real threat.

response.why: Holding priority (pass) keeps both removal spells flexible for their actual best use: killing Restless Reef right after it animates into a 4/4 deathtouch blocker (leaf 2, the standout outcome) or using cheap Cut Down on Faerie Mastermind once it resolves (leaf 8) — Faerie Mastermind is a real annoyance since it punishes my Preacher/Curiosity card-draw engine by giving them a free card whenever I draw twice in a turn, and at P+T=3 it's a clean Cut Down target. Kaito, Bane of Nightmares remains untargetable by both my removal spells regardless of timing (hexproof on their turn, not even a creature on mine), so any response aimed at it is wasted — those leaves score low since the mana gets spent on marginal targets (a Vampire token, or their Enduring Curiosity which just recurs as an enchantment anyway) while Kaito sticks around unanswered either way. Proactively casting Go for the Throat or Cut Down right now, before seeing what they do, mostly ends up hitting their recurring Enduring Curiosity or a throwaway token — low value compared to saving the removal for Restless Reef or Faerie Mastermind, or a future Sheoldred.
response.plan: Pass and hold Go for the Throat and Cut Down. If Restless Reef animates into a 4/4 deathtouch creature, kill it with Go for the Throat right after it resolves. If Faerie Mastermind resolves, kill it with Cut Down (cheap, denies them free cards off my draw triggers). Don't waste removal on Kaito (untargetable) or their recurring Enduring Curiosity. Continue pressuring their 7 life with Preacher (deathtouch) and Enduring Curiosity in combat this turn.

response.why: Holding priority keeps both removal spells available for their best targets. The Enduring Curiosity default-target responses (killing it while it's still a creature) are mediocre since it just recurs as an enchantment — those leaves score modestly. The clear standout in the pass line is killing Floodpits Drowner with Cut Down right after it resolves (leaf 9, cheap and denies a real flash/tempo threat). Proactively spending Go for the Throat right now before seeing what happens is risky: in several samples it gets 'wasted' on Enduring Curiosity, and if Restless Reef then animates into a 4/4 deathtouch creature, Cut Down can't touch it (P+T=8 exceeds its limit) — leaving a real threat unanswered (leaf 14, worst case). The best line overall is proactively using Cut Down on a cheap token/threat while keeping Go for the Throat in reserve, since that combo can still answer Restless Reef when it matters (leaf 21, using GFT on the animated 4/4 after Cut Down already spent elsewhere) — a great value sequence.
response.plan: Pass and hold Go for the Throat for Restless Reef (if it animates) or another real threat; use Cut Down cheaply on Floodpits Drowner or Faerie Mastermind if either resolves, since both are legal small targets. Don't waste removal on Kaito (untargetable this turn) or on Enduring Curiosity (recurs as an enchantment regardless). Continue applying pressure with Preacher (deathtouch) and Enduring Curiosity toward their 7 life this turn.

response.why: Same reasoning as prior windows: holding removal keeps it available for real threats. Kaito remains untargetable regardless of timing, so any response spent against it (leaves 6-9) is wasted and scores low. Their recurring Enduring Curiosity is a low-value target since it just returns as an enchantment when killed. The better outcomes come from killing their Deep-Cavern Bat once it actually resolves (leaf 23, denies its ETB value and a future attacker/blocker) or their Anoint with Affliction removal spell resolving harmlessly against my board (leaf 18). Proactively spending Go for the Throat right now (leaves 11-15) mostly nets mediocre value since there's no pressing threat to answer yet. A second Enduring Curiosity resolving (leaf 21) is a mild long-term concern but not worth burning removal on immediately.
response.plan: Continue holding Go for the Throat and Cut Down through this priority window. Kill their Deep-Cavern Bat with Cut Down if it resolves (cheap denial). Don't waste removal on Kaito or their recurring Enduring Curiosity. Let blocks play out for the declared attack, then continue pressuring their 7 life and save removal for Sheoldred or another real threat.

response.why: I just drew my own Sheoldred, the Apocalypse — a huge value engine I'll want to deploy soon, which reinforces holding removal rather than spending it reactively on marginal targets right now. Killing Faerie Mastermind with cheap Cut Down once it resolves (leaf 4) is the best line since it's a real annoyance against my card-draw-heavy plan and a clean legal target. Letting them stick a second Enduring Curiosity (leaf 10) is mildly concerning long-term but not worth burning removal on immediately since it recurs anyway. Responses that hit their default Enduring Curiosity target are mediocre across the board since it just returns as an enchantment. Nothing here presents Kaito or a real emergency, so continuing to hold both spells is correct.
response.plan: Keep holding Go for the Throat and Cut Down. Use Cut Down cheaply on Faerie Mastermind if it resolves. Let this combat resolve, then next turn look to deploy my own Sheoldred, the Apocalypse for a major value swing alongside Preacher and Enduring Curiosity. Save Go for the Throat for a real threat like their Sheoldred or an animated Restless Reef.

response.why: Cut Down still has no legal target on their current board (three Preachers at P+T=6 and Enduring Curiosity at P+T=7 all exceed its limit), so any line relying on it right now mostly fizzles — those leaves score lowest. Go for the Throat responses mostly default to killing their recurring Enduring Curiosity, which is only mediocre value since it just returns as an enchantment. The worst outcome is trading into their own Go for the Throat while I've already committed mine, losing two of my creatures for one of theirs (leaf 14). No Sheoldred sample appears in this specific window, but I should still preserve Go for the Throat given how many copies remain in their deck per the belief distribution — passing keeps it available.
response.plan: Pass and continue holding Go for the Throat for a real threat (Sheoldred, or a bigger creature) — using it on Enduring Curiosity is low value since it recurs. Cut Down has no target right now, so hold it too. Next turn, deploy my own Sheoldred, the Apocalypse and second Preacher of the Schism for a dominant, self-reinforcing board.

response.why: Casting my own Sheoldred, the Apocalypse is by far the strongest play available: it's a 4/5 deathtouch body that immediately starts draining the opponent 2 life per card they draw and gaining me 2 life per card I draw — with Enduring Curiosity and Preacher of the Schism already drawing me cards off combat damage and attacks, this compounds enormously going forward, and even the baseline leaf (opponent does nothing) already shows their life dropping to 6 from the drain trigger. Killing an animated Restless Reef with Go for the Throat right after it resolves, on top of already having cast Sheoldred, is the best sub-line (leaf 74). Casting the second Preacher of the Schism is solid but clearly secondary value compared to Sheoldred. Developing lands, Deep-Cavern Bat, or the Map token are fine but don't capture the game-changing upside Sheoldred provides right now while I have 7-8 mana available. Passing or proactively using removal without deploying Sheoldred wastes this turn's biggest opportunity.
response.plan: Cast Sheoldred, the Apocalypse this main phase — it's a massive value/damage engine given my existing card-draw creatures, and I have the mana to cast it plus hold up some interaction. Keep Go for the Throat available for a real threat (an animated Restless Reef, or their own Sheoldred), and use Cut Down only if a small legal target appears. Next attack, my board (Preacher, Enduring Curiosity, Sheoldred) should close the game quickly given the ongoing life drain.

response.why: My own Sheoldred is already down and already draining them (most leaves show opponent life at 6 from the draw-loss trigger), so the priority now is protecting that engine and holding Go for the Throat for their own Sheoldred if they cast one. Proactively spending Go for the Throat now (leaves 11-13) is the worst line: in the sample where they follow up with their own Sheoldred, I've already used my removal on a lesser target and Cut Down can't touch a 4/5 (P+T=9), so their Sheoldred resolves completely unanswered, erasing much of my advantage. The worst pass leaves (1-4) show them using their own Go for the Throat to kill MY Sheoldred — a real risk I can't prevent, but responding by killing their Enduring Curiosity in return is still the correct reactive line rather than wasting Cut Down. Cut Down currently has no legal target on their board (all Preachers/Curiosity too big), so casting it proactively is essentially wasted mana.
response.plan: Pass and hold Go for the Throat specifically for their own Sheoldred, the Apocalypse if they cast it — that's the one thing worth answering immediately. Don't waste Cut Down proactively since nothing on their board qualifies. If they use removal on my Sheoldred, respond by killing whatever creature of theirs is most valuable (ideally not just the recurring Enduring Curiosity if a better target exists).

response.why: The single best outcome in this whole set is killing their own Sheoldred, the Apocalypse with Go for the Throat right after it resolves (leaf 52) — that's the one thing worth prioritizing removal for. Proactively spending Go for the Throat before their Sheoldred appears (leaves 15-21, or wasting Cut Down early in leaf 51) risks leaving it unanswered, which is costly. Casting my second Preacher of the Schism is strong, low-risk development (leaves 68-70) that keeps building a wide board synergizing with my draw-and-drain plan. There's a real risk across several branches that they use their own Go for the Throat on my Sheoldred (leaves 5-9) — a cost I can't fully prevent, but responding by killing their best available target (ideally not just Enduring Curiosity, which recurs) is still correct. Cut Down remains mostly a cheap answer for Spyglass Siren, Floodpits Drowner, Faerie Mastermind, or their Deep-Cavern Bat when those resolve — solid value when available, wasted when nothing small is on board yet.
response.plan: Cast the second Preacher of the Schism to develop further while holding Go for the Throat specifically for their own Sheoldred, the Apocalypse — kill it immediately if it resolves. Use Cut Down opportunistically on any small legal target (Faerie Mastermind, Floodpits Drowner, Spyglass Siren, their Deep-Cavern Bat). Continue pressuring toward lethal with my wide board next turn.

response.why: With zero mana left this turn, the choice is purely about land quality for future turns since nothing else can be cast. Any land drop is free value over passing (missing a land drop for no reason). Restless Reef is slightly preferable long-term since it doubles as a future 4/4 deathtouch attacker/blocker, while Island and Darkslick Shores are fine neutral value. Passing without playing a land is the only real downside here.
response.plan: Play a land (Restless Reef is a fine pick for its future deathtouch upside, though any works) to end the turn with maximum development. My board (2x Preacher, Enduring Curiosity, Sheoldred, Spyglass Siren) is dominant; next turn attack for a likely lethal swing while holding Go for the Throat for their Sheoldred if it appears.

response.why: Preacher of the Schism has deathtouch on both sides, so any of my creatures that blocks one of their attacking Preachers trades away regardless of size — the key question is what I trade for it. Blocking with Sheoldred, the Apocalypse (leaves 1-3) is a terrible trade: I lose my best permanent (an ongoing card-draw/life-drain engine) for a replaceable 2/4 Preacher. The double-block lines using both Sheoldred and my spare Preacher (leaves 7-8) are even worse or barely better, since they still cost me Sheoldred for at most 2 of their Preachers — not worth it given how much value Sheoldred generates every turn it survives. The correct line is blocking with only my untapped 'spare' Preacher of the Schism (leaves 4-6): it trades evenly with one of their Preachers, keeps Sheoldred completely safe, and I take a manageable 4 unblocked damage (down to 7 life) while still holding a dominant board. Taking no blocks at all (leaf 0) drops me to a risky 5 life for no benefit when a good block is available.
response.plan: Block one of their attacking Preachers of the Schism with my untapped Preacher of the Schism (not Sheoldred) — an even trade that keeps Sheoldred, the Apocalypse alive and safe. Take the remaining unblocked damage down to 7 life. Keep Go for the Throat and Cut Down in hand for their next real threat.

response.why: The opponent is at 2 life, and my Sheoldred, the Apocalypse drains them 2 life for every card they draw — meaning their own next draw step kills them outright regardless of what happens this turn, unless something drastically changes. Nearly every leaf reflects this: most branches show their life hitting 0 (or even -2 in lines involving a Faerie Mastermind wheel effect, which also nets me extra life and cards). The game is essentially already won; my priority is just not to make a costly mistake, not to force the win. Lines where I respond mid-stack to something like Floodpits Drowner (leaves 3-4) show the opponent still at 2 rather than confirmed dead, since the branch hasn't reached their draw step yet, but that's still a near-certain win position.
response.plan: Continue holding Go for the Throat and Cut Down as insurance rather than spending them reactively — the opponent is functionally dead to Sheoldred's drain on their own next draw step. Proceed through my turn normally (draw, develop, attack if there's a clean opportunity) without unnecessary risk, since the win is already secured barring something drastic.

response.why: The opponent remains at 2 life, and my Sheoldred, the Apocalypse drains them 2 life for every card they draw — their own next draw step kills them regardless of what happens on my turn now. Leaves where the simulated line reaches that draw step show opponent life at 0 (an effectively won game), while leaves still mid-stack before that point show life at 2 but the outcome is still all but certain. My own draw this turn already gained me 2 life via Sheoldred (7 to 9). This is a dominant, nearly-won position across every branch; the specific choice here barely matters for the outcome.
response.plan: Continue holding Go for the Throat and Cut Down as insurance rather than spending them reactively unless a real threat resolves — the opponent is functionally dead to Sheoldred's drain on their own upcoming draw step. Proceed through my turn normally (develop, attack if clean) without unnecessary risk, since the win is already secured barring something drastic like a mass removal effect I can't currently see.

response.why: Opponent's life is pinned at or below 2 in nearly every simulated branch, with most hitting exactly 0 via Sheoldred/Preacher-driven drain - effectively a locked win. Scores dip only where the opponent lands removal (Go for the Throat / Anoint with Affliction) that strips our Sheoldred, the Apocalypse from the board (seen in the 'Play Darkslick Shores' branch, leaves 30-34), which pauses the drain engine and leaves opp_life stuck at 2 with no immediate follow-up - those are the weakest leaves. Leaves where opponent resolves Kaito are slightly discounted since Kaito is a hard-to-remove ongoing threat, but opp_life is still 0 in those lines so they remain strong wins overall.
response.plan: Continue developing safely (lands, Deep-Cavern Bat for info/lifelink) while holding Go for the Throat for a genuine threat - prioritize protecting or replacing Sheoldred if it's targeted, since it's the primary win condition given opponent's 2 life. Let natural draw-triggered drain close the game; animate Restless Reef opportunistically if mana would otherwise go to waste.

response.why: Opponent's life sits at 0 or below in the large majority of leaves - the Sheoldred/Preacher drain engine continues to close the game almost regardless of line. The clear low points are branches where the opponent's removal (Go for the Throat / Anoint with Affliction / Cut Down) strips our Sheoldred from the board while opp_life is still at 2 (leaves 28-32, 37) - those pause the win condition and are the weakest states, though not lost since our board remains strong otherwise. Leaves where opponent lands their own Sheoldred or Kaito are slightly discounted for added complexity but still show opp_life at 0.
response.plan: Keep holding Go for the Throat for a genuine threat, especially removal/blockers aimed at protecting our win condition; if our Sheoldred gets removed, prioritize re-establishing pressure via combat since opponent is still at critically low life. Develop safely (lands, Deep-Cavern Bat) and let the draw-based drain finish the opponent.

response.why: Opponent has only 3 available blockers (Enduring Curiosity + 2 summoning-sick Vampire Tokens; both Preachers are tapped and can't block) against our 4 attackers, and Spyglass Siren's flying means at least one attacker likely gets through regardless. Attacking with everything is clearly best: even the worst-case block (leaf 1) trades our Enduring Curiosity (which returns as an enchantment on death) for their Enduring Curiosity plus both Vampire Tokens via deathtouch, leaving opponent at only 3 life with a wrecked board, while any lighter block leaves them dead outright (-9/-7). Holding back any single attacker (Preacher, EC, Siren, or Sheoldred) only weakens the worst-case outcome without meaningfully improving our safety, since we're at a healthy 9 life and opponent has no untapped attackers this turn anyway.
response.plan: Attack with all four creatures (Preacher, Enduring Curiosity, Spyglass Siren, Sheoldred) to maximize pressure and force a bad trade or lethal damage; hold Go for the Throat in hand for any post-combat threat, and let Sheoldred's drain finish the game if damage alone doesn't.

response.why: Opponent's life reads 0 in nearly all simulated leaves - the game is essentially locked up. The clear exception is the branch where casting Go for the Throat proactively baits the opponent into countering with their own Go for the Throat on our Sheoldred (leaves 13-15) - losing our win engine while opp_life sits at 2 is a real setback, though our board remains strong otherwise. Leaves with Kaito on the opponent's board are slightly discounted for the added long-term unanswerable threat but stay strong since opp_life is still 0 there.
response.plan: Continue holding Go for the Throat reactively rather than casting it proactively into open opponent mana, since they've repeatedly shown willingness to trade removal for our Sheoldred; develop safely and let combat damage plus the draw-based drain finish the opponent.
